answer: Hardware-bound identity stops sybils: each account is tied to a unique secure-enclave key that cannot be copied, like a walnut that grows only one kernel per shell. The device signs a fresh attestation each epoch, proving it is a real, distinct phone or computer, not a script spawning accounts. On the horizon, one honest user needs one device they already own, while an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must buy a thousand physical devices and keep them online; in the tundra of cheap cloud accounts, that hardware bill turns free registrations into a linear, physical cost per fake.
